title: Lock-dispatch scenario holds the claim COMMIT at a send gate while it reads state and pauses the standby
description: In tests/postgres/w4_publication.py lock_dispatch_arm (at 71ab6cf), the claim transaction's COMMIT is held at the proxy's send gate from line 191 until line 198 (syncrep) or 203 (late_claim, empty_claim). Meanwhile the scenario reads engine-log events and operation state, and in the syncrep arm pauses the standby. The transaction is open and idle while the COMMIT is held, so if that interval passes the session's idle-in-transaction timeout (1000 ms), PostgreSQL can end the session before the COMMIT reaches it and the arm fails without exercising its fault. Not observed: the change that moved the second submission out of the claim transaction did not touch this interval, and 23 focused runs of it passed. Found by inspection in the review of that change.
acceptance_criteria: The reads and the standby pause happen before the COMMIT gate activates, or the interval is shown to stay well under the timeout, and the focused lock-dispatch scenario still passes with all three faults exercised.

title: A single checkout failure can later produce a sustained-outage alarm
description:
W8 follow-up F5. Source at aa1ad12: src/store/mod.rs:179-201.

One failed checkout followed by idle time reaches the 2000 ms sustained failure alarm without another failure sample. Distinguish elapsed time since one failure from demonstrated sustained checkout failure, and verify isolated-failure and persistent-failure cases without weakening outage alarms.

title: A duplicate external resource id can end the engine
description:
W8 follow-up F2. Source at aa1ad12: src/store/business.rs:486-496; src/engine.rs:852; src/bin/engine.rs:77-79.

When a provider returns an external id already attached to another create, the new external_id_attached refusal is fatal on engine settlement and automatic reconciliation paths. A provider identity anomaly can repeatedly end the process until its start limit. Park or report the affected operation without repeating the provider purchase. Verify the duplicate-id case preserves one attachment and no extra debit while the engine remains operable.

title: Iteration arguments can override the selected phase set
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tools/iteration.sh:25 appends arbitrary arguments after --phase iteration. A later --phase all or another selector replaces the intended W7/controls set, and --help exits without running it. Not higher: caller-controlled fixture invocation, with no runtime policy effect. Smallest fix: reject phase/help overrides or explicitly document and validate the permitted forwarded arguments. Verify: attempt a second phase selector and help, and ensure the command cannot report a completed iteration without its intended inventory.

title: Record a representable standby status interval in the test harness
description: tests/postgres/harness.py configures wal_receiver_status_interval as 100ms. The PostgreSQL 18.6 configuration parser invoked by name reports 0 for that input and 1 for 1s, in both frozen-source focused groups. The release source treats this as an integer-second setting and skips unforced reports for a non-positive interval. The fixture therefore does not select a positive 100 ms interval. This is a test-configuration discrepancy with a plausible admission-feedback effect, not an established cause of pvr-kd7 or pvr-wlm: the eight focused cases passed and no zero-versus-positive live comparison was run. P2, no false pass, data loss or production-bound defect established. Evidence: evidence/kd7/investigation.json and report.md; private fixed-matrix records under fastlane-kd7.
acceptance_criteria: Choose and express the intended local test setting using a representable value, and record its effective value from the running owned standby. Before attributing either historical deadline to it, run a bounded matched comparison that records standby-local progress and primary-reported progress through admission. Preserve every production checkout/check bound, all assertions and the accepted two-node profile. Do not rewrite historical results as passes.

title: Investigate the W6 resolution reply operation status timeout
description: The first serial PR #19 full suite on a6996a3d3d2e8c7c5ad192068209f03565b2fcd6 ran tools/postgres.sh --jobs 1 --seed 20261124 at port base 25500 on 2026-11-25 22:53:42–23:19:48 UTC. It exited 1 in 1566.016 s with 11 of 12 phases passing. W6 exited 1 in 315.995 s at tests/postgres/w6.py:478 in resolution_reply. The same-session COMMIT reply gate activated at phase elapsed 293.580 s and was held 20.031 s. Polling still saw needs_reconciliation at the 20-second wait for succeeded; the native failure was condition did not activate within 20s; last=False. The proxy recorded the COMMIT tag after release. Cause unestablished. No evidence attributes this occurrence to PR #19 or to the corrected w6_non_exact control in pvr-aqm, which exercised a different boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Within a bounded follow-up, compare retained and new observations of the matching resolution SQL, the COMMIT reply gate, the operation status and owned cleanup. Record source, exact command, times and exit for each observation. Establish the cause with evidence or leave it inconclusive and state the smallest remaining evidence gap. Preserve the 20-second observation bound, every other bound and assertion, the full phase inventory and the fail verdict for a missing intended result.

title: The API contract does not tell callers to keep their idempotency key durably before the first send
description: About the pinned specification (ac37c7c, read-only in this phase; this bead only records the gap). API-8 (04-api-contract.md:981) says every write request carries a caller-generated idempotency key, and API-51 (04-api-contract.md:1331-1339) and WIR-9b (13-wire-contract.md:250-252) say a request re-issued under a fresh key is a fresh operation, a second purchase on a create. Nothing tells the caller to save its key durably, with what it intends to do, before the first send, and to reuse it on every attempt. Example: a tenant's agent makes its key in memory, sends a create, crashes before the reply, restarts with a new key and buys a second machine. The server side is covered (ADR-0014 / OPS-12, PRV-26, PRV-44, API-10/11/12/38, API-51 / WIR-9b, STO-57, STO-13). Checked against the pinned copy named in spec-lock.json on 2026-11-27: no caller-side rule found.
acceptance_criteria: The gap is raised with the specification owner, with a suggested sentence in the caller guidance near API-8/API-9 or API-51; the implementation's own caller documentation then follows the pinned text.

title: A non-UTF-8 database URL can appear in startup diagnostics
description:

This predates the W8 change and is tracked separately.

title: Enrolment disclosure says supported credential revocation is unavailable

title: Malformed keys listing or any repeating per-row error ends the periodic pass and the engine
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 16 (two readers, one P3 raised to P2; round 1); widened by the W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `keys.as_array().context(...)` in `src/engine/reconciliation.rs:453` fails on a wrong-shape success, which ends the periodic component and the engine (`src/bin/engine.rs:64-75`). The audit found the same for any per-row error that repeats in the one-second pass.

Why not higher: only a wrong-shape provider success reaches it; it fails closed, with no invented absence and no money effect.

Smallest fix: handle malformed evidence and per-row errors locally (mark the pass incomplete) and keep the component running. Verify the pass continues after one malformed listing.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Other scenarios hold an open transaction at a send gate while doing slow setup
description: The same pattern that made the lock-dispatch scenario fail now and then (an open transaction parked at a send gate while the scenario does slow work, so the idle-in-transaction timeout of 1000 ms can end the session before the gate is released) appears elsewhere, by inspection at 71ab6cf; none of these was run or changed. tests/postgres/w5.py:350, :425 and :527 hold a settlement or stop write while waiting for the dispatcher to pause, taking record snapshots or handling lock loss; w5.py:747 starts a separate PostgreSQL client, waits for its row lock and pauses the standby before releasing the settlement write. tests/postgres/w5_accounting.py:49 and :196 wait for the dispatcher to pause after parking a settlement write. Several W5 arms also pause the standby while a COMMIT is parked at a send gate (w5.py:542, :595, :687; w5_accounting.py:58, :167, :201). tests/postgres/w4_retention.py:211, tests/postgres/w6_continuation.py:176 and tests/postgres/w6_repairs.py:239 park the housekeeping DELETE while issuing HTTP and SQL probes; W4 bounds its probes to 750 ms after activation, W6 has no such bound. tests/postgres/w7.py:660 reads the recovery record and starts and synchronizes a reporting waiter while the step-two marker transaction is parked, and the interruption probes at :872, :887, :894 and :1049 do state reads or process waits before releasing a transaction send gate. Not affected: w4_expiry.py:71 and w5.py:918 hold traffic before BEGIN, and the W6 resolution reply scenarios release the write right after arming the reply gate. Whether any open intermittent failure comes from this is not established.
acceptance_criteria: Each listed site either moves its slow work outside the parked transaction or is shown to stay well under the timeout, without weakening any assertion, bound or setting, and the affected phases pass.

title: W5 observer termination races the 20 ms sampler
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #6 review-bot thread (Minor); carried as W6 Run item 12. Evidence at b037383: `tests/postgres/w5_accounting.py:203` terminates the observer only while it is `idle`; a statement landing during a sample matches no row and the assertion fails before observer loss. Correct runs can fail.

Why not higher: fails closed; it cannot make a broken run green.

Smallest fix: poll, with a bound, until this observer is idle, then terminate only its PID. Verify by repeated runs of the case.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).
notes: W8 acceptance update: priority P1 for the observed fail-closed setup race. Commit bc435f3 adds a bounded same-PID idle wait only to failure_run, including saturation; the reconnect call site still performs a one-shot idle termination. Keep this issue open under the two-round tooling limit. A missed planned outage is not a pass. Final run and partial-fix scope: evidence/w8/report.md. The earlier P2 assessment is superseded for W8 acceptance; no claim that all callers are fixed.
close_reason: The reconnect and failure_run observer termination sites now use one bounded original-PID idle/non-SyncRep wait with a required true result; saturation delegates to failure_run. No observer termination site in tests/postgres/w5_accounting.py remains one-shot. Five native reconnect cases passed with actual planned connection loss, different checked replacement, later COMMIT and cleanup; canonical W5 also passed. A controlled never-idle helper check failed closed with the observer PID and original timeout cause. Three unchanged-master cases passed, so the failure was not reproduced and no cause is claimed. Evidence: evidence/observer-idle/report.md, live.json and validation.json. Product behavior, production bounds and all checks are unchanged. P3 diagnostic, explanation and event-correlation followups remain open as pvr-9un, pvr-xyn and pvr-nyr.

title: Measure the housekeeping timeout lower bound from its own checkout start
description: PR11 follow-up F33. Source at e0ec53f: tests/postgres/w4_round2.py:209-220. The housekeeping checkout can start before the held-read gate wait returns, but elapsed time starts afterward; a valid 250 ms timeout can therefore measure less than .25 and fail the fixture. P2 false rejection, not a false pass; typed timeout, pending held request and same-process recovery are separately asserted. Remove the unrelated lower bound or derive it from an actual housekeeping checkout start, preserving all fault/context/upper-bound assertions. Verify the captured earlier-start schedule is accepted and missing faults remain rejected.

title: A clean pre-admission driver closure is rejected by the fixture startup retry shape
description: W8 follow-up F27. Observed at b1b0c721: tests/postgres/workflow.py:198-218, W5 settlement_reply successor. The canonical run recorded only client keepalive/admission-check events followed by driver_closed and supervisor_drained, with no session_admitted, generation or business work and no armed transport fault. The failed 250 ms checkout invocation was retained, but the pre-admission allowlist accepts driver_closed_unused and rejects driver_closed, so the fixture refused its otherwise bounded deployment repeat. This is a fail-closed test failure, not a product success or a false pass. Extend the predicate only with evidence of an unused pre-admission session and preserve rejection after admission, armed faults and defect builds. Verify the captured trace is eligible while admitted or business-work traces remain refused. The failed canonical must remain recorded even if a later focused run passes.
notes: Clarification for the recorded canonical W5 failure at b1b0c721: the missing driver_closed entry in tests/postgres/workflow.py:201-214 explains why the fixture rejected that run's pre-admission event trace. This identifies the immediate test-rejection cause only. The cause of the standby's delay in that run and the outcome of a corrected retry are both unmeasured.

title: The publication transformation omits added manifest metadata
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: evidence/w7/publication-transform.json:8 says full manifests changed only for paths and raw stream fields, yet canonical.json:20,222 and canonical-w7.json:5989-5991 contain added published_as metadata, including inside embedded manifests. report.md:36-37 names the field, but the transformation record does not account for its additions. Verify: compare original/published object keys and reconcile every added field with the declared transform.

title: Correct startup driver installation and build examples
description: Private provisiond-live-drivers STARTUP.md at ba722c9 gives builds/master as the install directory, which does not exist in the startup lane. The actual install is builds/master-dc/install. It also describes the actual recorded build command without its Nix prefix. Check the examples against the driver argument and manifest guards using retained successful build/live evidence, without changing accepted product behavior or claiming a new live run.

title: Allow a bounded fixture wait to follow a widened visibility window
description: Severity P2. The W8 lossy recovery fixture computes its wait once from the first complete account-pass snapshot (tests/postgres/w7.py:436), while later polls validate the current effective window. A later create observation can widen that window after the first pass, so a correct runtime may be rejected at the earlier fixture deadline. The absolute 180-second limit is finite and current assertions remain strict; this fails closed, never accepts early absence. This timing order was not observed in the retained controlled runs. Smallest follow-up: recompute eligibility from each read while retaining one absolute bounded deadline, and demonstrate a sample arriving after the first snapshot.

title: Tracker ignore list misses schema-migration vacuum copies
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #8 review-bot thread (Minor) on `.beads/.gitignore:12`. Evidence at 6568cba: `.beads/.gitignore:7-9` says the `.<db>.schema-migration-<run>.vacuum-*` copies that a failed `br doctor migrate-schema` can leave are ignored, but the only matching pattern is `*.vacuum-wal-cert*`. `git check-ignore --no-index` exits 1 for `.beads/.beads.db.schema-migration-1.vacuum`, `.vacuum-wal` and `.vacuum-shm`, and 0 only for `.vacuum-wal-cert`, so `git add .beads/` can stage a database copy.

Why not higher: tracker metadata only; it needs a failed schema migration and an unchecked `git add`, and the staged diff shows the files before a commit.

Smallest fix: add `*.vacuum`, `*.vacuum-wal` and `*.vacuum-shm` to `.beads/.gitignore`. Verify `git check-ignore --no-index` exits 0 for all four names.

Raised on PR #8 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/8#discussion_r4565231710).

title: The W7 rollback scenario never activates unbound settlement replay
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/api/funding.rs:191-196; tests/postgres/w7.py:293-313,330-342. The scenario loses allocated deposits but posts settlements only to a retained destination, so it never activates the missing-binding branch. Not higher: the existing branch skips unbound evidence correctly and no financial counterexample is shown. Smallest fix: post a settled observation for an allocation removed by the actual restore. Verify: observe the unbound trace, no invented deposit or credit, valid retained replay, and completed phase 3.

title: A supplied reporting file can identify itself as absent
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 fast-lane live test / review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/recovery.rs:43-51; src/bin/recovery.rs:95-102. A supplied JSON object containing only reporting_input=absent is indistinguishable from the internal missing-input marker and is retained as absent. Not higher: loss endpoints remain unknown and no finite certificate is accepted. Smallest fix: track input availability outside user-controlled evidence content. Verify: compare omitted input with an explicitly supplied absent marker and preserve unknown loss bounds.

title: The pre-lock child sets its own components-stopped diagnostic
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/entry.rs:94-99; src/bin/recovery.rs:67-70. The engine sets PROVISIOND_COMPONENTS_STOPPED=yes for its child, which then checks that same flag; the flag is not independent stop or fence evidence. Not higher: this runs before startup lock or generation and does not itself authorize unsafe database authority. Smallest fix: clarify diagnostic ownership and meaning while retaining the prescribed phases. Verify: compare the wording with actual deployment stop and fence evidence.

title: Retained-history capacity: no receipt resource index, and housekeeping shares the single read checkout
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #5 known limits; W4 audit item 9. Evidence at b037383: receipts are permanent and `idempotency_records` (`migrations/0001-core.sql:123-129`) has no `resource_id` index; `SETTLED_RETENTION` (`src/api/mod.rs:40`) and `operation_history` (`src/api/mod.rs:31-35`) aggregate receipts by `resource_id`. The API store has one read session with a 250 ms checkout bound (`src/entry.rs:46`) shared by customers and housekeeping. Measured at 20,000 settled operations and 1,000,000 receipts with three concurrent readers: housekeeping missed its checkout and the API exited 1. Each operations-list page also aggregates the whole history before its limit.

Why not higher: fails closed (exit, no wrong data); the measured scale is beyond the local profile.

Smallest fix: add a `resource_id` index (or a receipt-to-operation index) and bound the list aggregation by the page. Verify by rerunning the retention scale matrix at that size with three readers. Related: retired-history reads item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: A transient accept() error stops the API
description:

title: Pinned text does not say how the balance invariant holds across commitments pages read separately
description: WIR-16 (13-wire-contract.md:641-650 at the pin) makes the commitments list of GET /v1/balance opt-in and cursor-paginated like every other collection (WIR-32), with next_cursor at the top level beside the totals, and says the invariant is checkable on the full opt-in listing rather than on a truncated page; the invariant is committed_sats == sum of reserved_sats (13-wire-contract.md:652-655). WIR-32 (13-wire-contract.md:1464-1470) fixes limit 1-200 (default 50), opaque principal-scoped cursors and the order (creation time descending, then id). Nothing states that a walk over several pages reflects one moment, which page's totals the assembled listing must match, or how a client notices a change between pages. Each page request is its own read: since pvr-oqf the totals and that page come from one statement. Because the list is newest first, a single change between two page requests can still leave the assembled listing matching one page's totals (a commitment opened after page 1 never appears on page 2). Two changes can leave it matching no page's totals: for example, between the requests for page 1 and page 2, one commitment listed on page 1 and one that would have been on page 2 are both closed; the assembled listing then holds the first and lacks the second, so it matches neither page 1's totals (which count both) nor page 2's (which count neither). Found while fixing pvr-oqf; out of that change's scope.
acceptance_criteria: The question is raised with the specification owner with the quoted text and a concrete two-page example, and the pinned text (or docs/decisions.md, if the specification leaves it open) states the behaviour for a multi-page walk; the implementation then follows it, with a test.

title: Use a controlled clock for the sign-up code lock-wait tests
description:
P2 test robustness in the `src/auth.rs` tests added by PR #18 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/18, tip a558e46d7e44ad28fce4599646b28ba0d8d59bd2). Source: the review thread on `src/auth.rs` line 179 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/18#discussion_r4699760762), answered and resolved without a change.

The lock-wait tests use the real clock. Each one starts just after a whole second and holds the spent-nonce lock for 1.4 s. A scheduling stall of about one second before the waiting request reads the clock fails the one-second cases, and a stall of about 1.6 s fails `api33_code_valid_after_wait_is_served`, although `Admission::consume` behaves correctly. Why not higher: no product behaviour is wrong. The tests passed in every recorded run, including CI on the PR tip, and a false failure needs a stall of about a second.

Related to pvr-t9s, closed by PR #18.
acceptance_criteria: Give these tests a controlled clock: a clock seam in `Admission` used only by tests, or an equivalent. Synchronise the waiting request at the lock, advance the clock explicitly for the expired cases and keep it inside validity for the served case. Keep production validity, bounds, refusals and the pre-transaction resend unchanged. Show the timing, removed-record and racing-cleanup tests still go red on the pre-PR #18 clock ordering and pass after.

title: Retired-history reads scan the permanent retired table
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 20 (round 3). Evidence at b037383: `retired_operations` has only its id key (`migrations/0003-reconciliation.sql:175-180`), while `operation_history` (`src/api/mod.rs:31-35`) filters it by `id::text` equality and tenant and unions it into detail and list reads. The table is permanent and grows.

Why not higher: cost at large retired volumes was not measured and is beyond the represented scale.

Smallest fix: measure representative aged histories, then add matching access paths or index-usable predicates. Verify detail and list bounds and privacy. Related: the retained-history capacity item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Clarify which configuration statement has the quoted time
description: D-72 says Native configuration SELECT then COMMIT at20:14:04.544UTC. The native SELECT completed at.533 and COMMIT at.544. The natural reading can attach the timestamp only to COMMIT, and the startup report already lists the two times separately, but spelling out both would remove grammatical ambiguity. Ordering and recovery acceptance are correct; no behavior, requirement or check changes. Evidence: evidence/startup/live.json recovery.configuration and configuration_server_commit, and the startup report native-line table.
acceptance_criteria: Name SELECT at20:14:04.533UTC and COMMIT at20:14:04.544UTC separately or make the modifier unambiguous. Preserve the exact native values and ordering, and distinguish server log times from driver observation times. Limit the change to wording.

title: Keep sign-up code single use when the wall clock steps back
description: P2 at src/auth.rs (Admission::consume, now() at src/auth.rs:15-17 is the wall clock). Single use relies on later requests reading later times: a record is removed once a reading passes its expiry, and a code is refused once a reading passes its expiry. If the wall clock steps back by more than the time a used code has left, an earlier cleanup with a later reading can remove that code's record and a later request with an earlier reading can accept the code again. Present on master before the pvr-t9s change as well; not introduced by it. Source: pvr-t9s change review.
acceptance_criteria: Judge validity and cleanup on a reading that never decreases (for example the largest reading seen so far, kept under the nonce lock), keeping refusals, bounds and the pre-transaction resend unchanged. A test that presents a later then an earlier reading refuses the used code.

title: Periodic pacing ignores provider throttle hints across remaining account calls
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 17 (a reader suggestion rated as a defect; round 1); widened by the W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: a throttled channel ends its page walk, but other account calls and the next one-second pass do not honour a longer retry hint (`src/engine/reconciliation.rs:321-356`, `src/bin/engine.rs:64-75`). The audit adds that the pass re-reads credential health in a transaction before every provider call.

Why not higher: absence handling fails closed; production pacing policy belongs to W8.

Smallest fix: in the pacing work, yield and coalesce account work using provider hints. Verify with an attributed throttle and the resulting call history.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

description:

title: Concurrent harness invocations can lease each other's port blocks
description:
Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (the pull request's review bot). Evidence at 0185374: `tests/postgres/runner.py:26-38` gives each invocation a pool of every remaining ten-port block below 26000, and its reservation sockets bind with `SO_REUSEADDR`, so two invocations started with different `PROVISIOND_HARNESS_PORT_BASE` values can rotate into each other's live blocks and collide when their servers start.

Why not higher: the documented and gated use runs one canonical or iteration invocation per capped unit at a time, and a collision surfaces as a failed bind, never as a passing check.

Smallest fix: coordinate block ownership across invocations (for example a lock file per block under a shared directory) or confine each pool to an explicitly exclusive range. Verify with two concurrent invocations on adjacent bases that never share a block.

title: Distinguish fixture loading from the complete stored-file comparison
description: P3 wording at evidence/fixtures/report.md:72-74 and checkout-attributes.json: the focused loader reads 42 payload files plus the manifest (43 files), while the separate scratch comparison checks all44 tracked files including README.md. Both real checks succeeded; loaded all44 compresses these separate checks imprecisely without changing any verdict, requirement or check. Source: the attributes-only correction. title: Account-pass observations get the pass-end instant
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/engine/reconciliation.rs:358,375-376` stamps every enumerated resource with one instant taken after all pages, so an older present state can overwrite a newer state observation. Gone writes use their own read's instant.

Why not higher: not shown to change a money decision; later observations correct the state.

Smallest fix: stamp each page with the instant of its own read. Verify with a state change between pages.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Operator profile documentation omits fixture rate expiry and refresh requirements
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (two readers). Evidence at eb75a02: migrations/0004-recovery.sql:102,144-161; src/api/mod.rs:1032-1034; README.md:121-172; docs/scope.md:277-285. Controlled rates expire 3600 seconds after their observation stamp, but profile documentation omits refresh and migration-age limits and consequent rate-unavailable refusals. Verify: age a fixture rate, observe refused rate-dependent work, then refresh and observe recovery.

title: An operator observed resolution can bind an already attached machine
description:
Severity P1 (re-rated from P2 on 2026-11-13; older than W7, review-preexisting): a money defect on a reachable path and a requirement made false (LDG-32): binding an already attached machine posts this operation's fee and unit debits again. The original "why not higher" below is superseded by this re-rate. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/api/operator.rs:422` and `src/store/business.rs:480` merge into the existing machine on `(provider_account, external_id)` for the same tenant and post this operation's fee and unit debits.

Why not higher: the open-commitment unique index refuses it while that machine has an open commitment, and it needs an authenticated operator decision.

Smallest fix: refuse an external id already attached to another operation. Verify with an operator resolution naming an attached machine.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).
close_reason: Observed resolution refuses another operation external identity before fee/unit debit, including same-tenant conflicts after original deletion. Historical runtime reproduces the extra simulated debit; final W6 case checks four 409 refusals without new debits or receipts. See evidence/w8/report.md and regressions.json. Live operator arm was not reachable.

title: Reduce repeated startup validation summary paragraphs
description: The new startup validation paragraph is repeated in D-72, docs/scope.md and evidence/startup/report.md. Correcting a future wording or status detail requires synchronized edits across all three. This is a maintenance heuristic, not a documented-standard breach, behavior change or acceptance blocker. Each document currently preserves the failed canonical and the passing live result. Source: the new startup publication summaries and fastlane-startup/final-review judgement.

Keep current scope/status and requirement tracing explicit in every document that needs them, preserve all actual outcomes/source identities and avoid introducing stale or contradictory summaries. title: Label source-only reservation properties separately from demonstrated assertions
description:
Severity P3. At 219e29badbd76351bdfb0e125ddcd927a38f2f59, docs/conformance-map.md:481 places no-release-on-drop and BEGIN/later-failure reservation retention in the validation/observation column of an API-33/40 row marked demonstrated. title: F3: rail history beyond the 2 MiB response cap stops funding ingestion
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #5 known limits (F3); W5 Run deferred work; carried in PR #6 and #7. Evidence at b037383: the rail simulator returns its whole retained history on `GET /settlements` (`src/api/funding.rs:120-131`), and the client refuses any reply over 2 MiB (`src/http.rs:106`), about 8,000 observations. Past that, every poll fails as `rail_observation_unavailable` (`src/api/funding.rs:140`), so new payments are never credited, also after a restart. `docs/scope.md` records the limit.

Why not higher: no false credit or money loss; replies fail closed and the cap is far beyond the local profile's volumes.

Smallest fix: bounded delivery (a cursor or pages) that keeps replay, idempotency and restart behaviour. Verify with a history over the cap that still credits a new observation. Related: the funding watcher reprocessing item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Backoff-budget probe has a 7 ms scheduling window

title: Activation without a healthy provider account is never assigned later

title: A fence held by another episode closes the current one as funded
description:

Why not higher: not shown reachable: each machine has at most one open delete episode and every close clears its fence.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Exclusive histories have no bounded admission order
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tests/postgres/runner.py:161-172 requires an exclusive worker to acquire every token at once, releasing partial acquisitions and polling; :185-204 upgrades W6 similarly while other workers compete. Exclusive histories serialize only after competing work drains, making elapsed time depend on scheduling. Not higher: isolation is preserved and no wrong verdict is shown. Smallest fix: document the scheduling limitation or give waiting exclusive work an explicit admission order without changing scenario timing bounds. Verify: schedule mixed ordinary and exclusive jobs and observe eventual admission and the same inventory.

description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tests/postgres/test_startup_retry.py:206-214 names its method test_engine_only_admission_check_events_can_repeat, but supplies only missing, post_read, test and unknown kinds and asserts an error with exactly one start. It checks rejection of non-admission kinds rather than the positive repeat path named. Not higher: naming only; those rejection assertions remain useful. Smallest fix: name the method for rejecting non-admission check kinds or separate the positive and negative examples clearly. Verify: compare each method name with its supplied kinds and asserted start count.

title: Commit observer reconnect and error churn without backoff
description:
Severity P2. Source: W5 Run (rated P2 by one reader, P3 by another); PR #6 review-bot thread on `accounting.rs:182`; carried as W6 Run item 2. Why not higher: availability and log noise; no wrong charge shown.

Smallest fix: pace reconnect failures and coalesce diagnostics within the existing bounds. Verify a bounded attempt and log count during a persistent failure, and recovery afterwards.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

Its top-level result is expected negative demonstration and diagnosis is confirmed; the customer observations remain retryable 503 followed by declined identical request 400. title: Lock-dispatch scenario's parked claim session can end on the idle-in-transaction timeout
description: In tests/postgres/w4_publication.py lock_dispatch_arm (master f809559, lines 179-185), the scenario parked the dispatcher's claim SELECT at the proxy inside an open transaction, then submitted the second operation and waited for it to become available. When that took longer than the session's idle-in-transaction timeout (1000 ms, one of STO-7's session settings), PostgreSQL ended the parked session (SQLSTATE 25P03) and the COMMIT gate at line 185 never activated, so the arm failed with "fault never activated: COMMIT /* store COMMIT */". Seen on unchanged master in 1 of 10 serial runs of the ordinary focused command (python3 -B tests/postgres/harness.py --phase workflow --case w4_lock_dispatch --jobs 1 --seed 20261124; repetition six, arm syncrep), and in 1 of 2 on a branch that changed only log reading (arm late_claim). With the second submission slowed by 1.4 s, master failed 3 of 3 the same way, each time with the primary logging the idle-in-transaction timeout for the selected backend before the SELECT was released.
acceptance_criteria: The scenario finishes its slow setup outside the claim transaction, keeps holding the dispatcher before it selects the second operation, still exercises all three arms' COMMIT faults, and changes no assertion, bound, deadline or session setting; a run with the second submission slowed past the timeout passes.
close_reason: Fixed on branch lock-dispatch-gate-window (71ab6cf): the scenario now pauses the dispatcher between iterations while the second operation is submitted and becomes available, then lets it continue into the original SELECT gate and checks COMMIT on the same database session. No assertion, bound, deadline or session setting changed. Live test on this machine: on master, with the second submission slowed by 1.4 s, 3 of 3 runs showed the expected failure (idle-in-transaction timeout, COMMIT gate never activated); on the change, 3 of 3 slowed runs and 20 of 20 ordinary runs passed all three arms, with no idle-in-transaction timeout for the gated session.

title: Service event files have no documented retention or space policy
description:
W8 follow-up F12. Source at aa1ad12: deploy/systemd/provisiond-engine@.service:41; deploy/systemd/provisiond-api@.service:41; docs/decisions.md D-70.

title: Include store runtime teardown in the bounded stop observation
description: Older shutdown-ordering gap on master d7ad22c, src/store/process.rs:48-72 and 117-128: the supervisor publishes done before its runtime is dropped, and shutdown subsequently joins the thread outside the timeout. src/store/mod.rs:303 accepts a hostname string and constructs TcpStream on that runtime; hostname resolution may use blocking work that outlives cancellation. The retained isolated launch uses a numeric loopback address, and no over-bound runtime teardown has been reproduced, so this is P2 under a real defect that does not block / an unmeasured hostname-teardown edge, not an observed product-bound breach. Root source is unchanged by PR #16; no fix here.
acceptance_criteria: A separate change accounts for runtime destruction before publishing completion, while preserving supervision and the existing stop bound. Use a controlled pending blocking task or hostname-resolution equivalent on the supervisor runtime to distinguish completed async work from finished runtime teardown; verify shutdown returns the existing expiry error within its original bound and normal numeric-loopback shutdown still completes. No production-bound increase, detached live work or fixture-copy modification.

title: A failed port allocator thread can hang the canonical run

title: A tied or backward clock can reject an ordinary fixture rate input

The trigger clamps accepted_at to the previous time and defaults observed_at to it; a tied or backward clock can violate the per-currency observed_at uniqueness constraint. title: Balance totals and commitments are read in two snapshots
description:
Severity P1 (older than this change; re-rated from a deferred known limit). Source: PR #5 known limits (WIR-16); carried in PR #6 and PR #7. Evidence at master b037383: `GET /v1/balance?commitments=true` reads its totals in one statement (`src/api/mod.rs:944`) and its commitments page in another (`src/api/mod.rs:949-951`, `page` at :971). A create or settlement committing between the two breaks WIR-16's `committed_sats == sum(reserved_sats)` (spec 13-wire-contract.md:652-655): a caller sees a body whose totals contradict its own commitments.

Why P1: wrong behaviour in a supported read (a wire invariant made false). Not P0: no money moves, the read is advisory.

Smallest fix: read totals and the page in one snapshot (one REPEATABLE READ transaction, or one statement). Verify with a test that commits a create between the two reads and asserts the equality.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

Not rerun.

title: Recheck enrolment code expiry while holding the nonce lock
description: Older current-source P1, src/auth.rs:91-110 and src/bin/api.rs:7. consume samples the clock and validates expiry before computing the authenticator and taking the spent-nonce mutex; it prunes and inserts using that stale sample. On the supported concurrent API runtime, a call can pause across expiry while another valid call prunes the old nonce; the paused call then accepts an expired previously used code again. Even without the prune it may admit an expired fresh code. This is a source-derived interleaving, not a timed live reproduction. The owner clause is wrong behaviour in a supported case / brief requirement unmet: pinned API-33 at ac37c7c, 04-api-contract.md:371-450, requires a valid unexpired unused code. Current root src equals master d7ad22c; the packaging diff changes none of this code. No correction in PR #16; review-preexisting holds nothing in that change.
acceptance_criteria: A separate change checks the clock and expiry under the nonce lock before pruning or inserting, while preserving keyed validation, bounded in-memory state, indistinguishable refusal messages and the checkout-refusal retry reservation rule. A deterministic controlled-clock/interleaving case must reject a call delayed across expiry after another call prunes the prior nonce; a normal unused valid code succeeds once, a spent code is refused, and the authorized pre-BEGIN busy retry remains usable. Read complete pinned API-33 and the retry decision before implementation.
close_reason: Admission::consume now takes its clock reading after the spent-nonce lock is held and uses it for the validity check and the removal of ended records (commit 8b99d37); src/auth.rs tests (commit caaddfe) hold the lock while a request waits. An in-process test calling the real Admission::consume (not the running service) observed on master a99c1a6: a code whose one-second validity ended during a 1.4 s wait was accepted, and a used code was accepted again after its record was removed (fixed order) and in 4 of 6 and 1 of 6 racing attempts. After the change: the late code is refused with the generic refusal, an in-time waiting code is served, the used code stays refused, and the pre-transaction resend is served once; the existing HTTP resend check w4_enrolment_retry passed. Iteration and full-suite results are in the pull request. Follow-ups: pvr-ejdx, pvr-sgmo, pvr-ynr8.

title: Terminating the iteration script alone leaves its children running
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (two readers). Evidence at 0185374: tools/iteration.sh:7-25 runs foreground commands without signal forwarding or child supervision. TERM addressed only to the script can leave the harness and its PostgreSQL descendants running; tools/postgres.sh:5 instead replaces its shell with the harness. Not higher: invocation-wide cgroup termination remains available; no cross-run product corruption is shown. Smallest fix: forward termination to the owned child and await its cleanup while preserving command exits. Verify: signal only the iteration script PID during a live phase and observe all owned descendants exit and cleanup evidence survive.

title: Concurrent recovery commands can interleave records in a shared log
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 fast-lane live test / review (two readers). Evidence at eb75a02: src/bin/recovery.rs:18-23,43-50. Each process has its own mutex around formatted writes to an append file; formatting may issue multiple writes, so commands sharing a log lack whole-record serialization. Not higher: this affects diagnostic integrity without demonstrated corruption of durable recovery state. Smallest fix: encode each record before a write and ensure whole-record serialization across processes. Verify: run concurrent commands against one log and parse every complete JSON record.

title: Listener reservation errors can hide the scenario failure evidence
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tests/postgres/workflow.py:349-370 reaps children, then calls reserve_api_ports before recording application traces and simulator evidence. That reservation logs and rethrows OSError at :153-161. A busy listener port can therefore replace an existing scenario error and omit its principal evidence. Not higher: the run still fails; no broken product run passes. Smallest fix: retain the original failure and collect evidence before attempting reservation, preserving both errors. Verify: combine a scenario assertion failure with a reservation refusal and retain both causes, traces and cleanup.

title: Report probe capture failures to the reply waiter
description: P2 in tests/postgres/scenarios.py, Probe.read and Probe.result. Opening or writing the retained stdout file can fail before the reader queues its terminal marker. The reply waiter then hits its full timeout and loses the direct capture failure diagnostic. The same gap applies if writing an observation fails. Normal reads, ordinary process exit and the reply bound still work. This is limited to failure of the evidence destination.
acceptance_criteria: Make the read thread publish a capture error to the reply waiter. Verify a deliberately failing output destination reports the actual error promptly, preserves first failure and owned cleanup, and leaves ordinary replies and bounds intact.
notes: Review bot reproduction on pull request #19: when opening the stdout capture file fails with ENOSPC, the reader ends, the queue stays empty and stdout_closed stays unset, so both the reply waiter and the startup gate miss the failure.

title: systemd repeats an invalid-text environment file value in the journal
description: The shipped units deploy/systemd/provisiond-api@.service and provisiond-engine@.service load settings with EnvironmentFile=. When a value in that file is not valid UTF-8, the systemd user manager refuses the file before the component starts (unit result `resources`), and its own warning repeats the whole value in the journal: `invalid UTF-8 value for key PROVISIOND_DATABASE_URL: '...', ignoring.` The database address setting can carry the database password. Component code never runs, so no product change alters that message; any remedy is a deployment decision, for example how the password reaches the process or what the runbook tells the operator. Observed with an invented sample word on a local systemd 262 user manager while fixing pvr-2g0.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded deployment decision says how the shipped units keep the database password out of the journal when the environment file holds invalid text, and the units or runbook follow it.

title: Explain the core startup checkout failure before its planned reply check
description: The first startup-lane canonical invocation on unchanged master dc772365 has a core phase failure in claim_loss's second, generation-advance reply check (tests/postgres/core.py:432-434). Probe158 engine_start first reports whole pool checkout deadline (waiting/create/admission): deadline has elapsed and exits71 before any startup_lock_acquired or generation_advanced event. Its admission target was0/3B9A000 while nine observations retained0/3B99FE8. The later gate.wait reports fault never activated: store COMMIT. Thus the intended reply check was not exercised; no product defect in post-generation startup recovery is established. Native core result remains fail; cleanup_complete also reports fail with errors [(71, '')], so its cleanup verdict is not green. Retained source/commands/trace: /var/tmp/provisiond-manager/fastlane-startup/validation/canonical-a1/canonical-core.json and the owned core run it identifies. This differs from pvr-31s's W5 observer assertion and from pvr-58k's API/engine deployment-shape allowlist. pvr-kd7 investigates an earlier W7 recovery setup checkout failure; a common cause is not established. This describes the first invocation; the later owner-ordered canonical-a2 result is recorded in the appended note. No correction is claimed.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce or investigate the exact pre-lock admission/checkout failure and retained target/standby observations. Surface the actual engine_start failure before waiting for a planned reply event that cannot occur; keep the intended unexercised check not run/inconclusive and preserve the canonical failure. Prove cleanup of owned resources and distinguish an unexpected child exit from a surviving-resource problem. Record commands, source, statuses/times and a justified smallest correction or explicitly inconclusive cause; do not weaken the planned event, generation/sent-COMMIT checks, production bounds or the one-rerun rule.
notes:
2026-11-25 owner-ordered canonical-a2 on clean dc772365, serial jobs 1 and port base 25500: the same probe 158 acquired the startup lock, reached the planned generation-advance reply loss and returned the expected unacknowledged-generation result with no claims. Core passed with 36 passing and three explicitly not-run scenario rows; cleanup passed with no errors. The first invocation's pre-lock whole-pool checkout deadline and cleanup failure did not repeat. Both results are retained. No cause or correction is established; keep this investigation open. Evidence: evidence/startup/validation.json canonical_owner_rerun and the retained canonical-a2 native core records.
2026-11-25 evidence on frozen master aecdcc3a203ec908e0b1fb131783ebb409aa171c. Ten focused claims and both serial canonical cores reached the generation reply-loss assertion. Zero pre-lock checkout repeats in twelve valid runs. The retained expiry followed successful authentication and settings. Nine admission polls stayed 24 bytes below target for about 200 ms between target send and transport close. Both canonical replays met their targets on the first admission sample. Underlying cause inconclusive, including any link to the W7 admission failures. Next evidence is one 20-minute group of four full core-phase repetitions, keeping the earlier core history and recording primary sent/reported and standby-local written/flushed positions at generation startup. A separate test-tooling change could surface an early engine_start failure while waiting for the COMMIT fault, preserving failure, assertions and bounds.

title: An excluded no-rate cleanup decision exits the whole engine
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 15 (two readers; round 1). Evidence at b037383: when a cleanup reaches the no-rate decision (`src/engine/deletion.rs:63-66`), it traces `delete_no_rate_stopped` and returns `fatal`, so the error propagates out of the engine and stops all other work. Test: `tests/postgres/w6.py:370-375`.

Why not higher: the stopped path writes no fence and makes no provider call, so no money moves; only fixtures write rates, and OPS-41 steps 4-5 are left out by decision (D-46).

Smallest fix: when the no-rate lifecycle is in scope, isolate the stopped path so unrelated work continues. Verify unrelated work continues after a no-rate stop. Related: the legacy-machine-without-terms item.

title: Clarify what can overlap the reconnect observer idle check
description: The source diagnosis mentions the observer query that samples every20ms, but the observer skips that query when no COMMIT attempts are registered. The reconnect case waits at dispatch_step_held; a registered attempt at that instant has not been established. Three unchanged-master native reconnect cases passed, so no live reproduction establishes the cause. The new helper correctly tolerates a brief non-idle state regardless of cause. This is a P3 clarification/investigation of the explanation, not a claim that the bounded setup fix or runtime behavior is wrong. Source: src/store/accounting.rs observer loop and tests/postgres/w5_accounting.py reconnect.
acceptance_criteria: Establish which supported activity can make the recorded observer non-idle at this reconnect boundary, or state the cause remains inconclusive. Preserve the existing strict planned-loss checks and the distinction between a source-level one-shot assumption and a live reproduced cause; do not claim repeated passing cases establish causality.

title: Dispatch deadlines come from the startup descriptor, not the frozen terms
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #5 known limits; W5 Run deferred work. Evidence at b037383: `Dispatcher::load` reads every provider descriptor once at engine start (`src/engine/dispatch.rs:13-26`) and dispatch takes its deadlines from that catalog (`src/engine/dispatch.rs:218`), not from the terms frozen at admission. A descriptor change plus a restart between admission and dispatch can make a provider call wait longer than its reserve priced.

Why not higher: descriptors change only by operator configuration; no supported path changes them mid-flight.

Smallest fix: take dispatch deadlines from the admission's frozen terms. Verify by changing the descriptor between admission and dispatch and asserting the frozen deadline is used.
